why: Each attribute is one level of a decision tree and each allowed value is a branch; a depth-first walk that picks one value per key in order emits the Cartesian product with the first attribute changing slowest. It is the same tree as Letter Combinations of a Phone Number.
hints: How does this compare to choosing one letter per phone digit?
DFS over attribute index i: for each value in values[i] in order, append it, recurse to i + 1, pop. When i == len(keys), record a copy of the row.
Output size is the product of list lengths (<= 10^5), and the DFS does O(len(keys)) work per row. An iterative build (start with [[]], extend by each attribute) works too.
pitfalls: No keys means one empty assignment: return [[]].
Any attribute with an empty value list means no assignments at all: return [].
Keep the given order of values; do not sort them.
